title: Fleet setup outputs: what `workspace:setup` produces is restored from the fleet when a machine of the same class already produced it, keyed by the content of its real inputs
description: A setup task writes into a host store (dependency store, cargo home, tools partition). Its output is a function of (a) the real inputs: lockfiles, pins, tool versions, toolchain channel, (b) the class of the host that built it: `neutral` (text that is byte-identical everywhere), `posix` (the class of graph-state/platform-class: darwin and linux share it; only for trees that hold no native code) and `host` (OS, architecture and libc: anything that holds a native binary). A record is stored beside the install packs of the group store (space `setup`), signed by the publishing origin, verified by digest and by the per-file fingerprint when restored, and placed into the real directory by rename, so a restore is complete or a miss.

CargoTools.description: The executables `cargo install --locked <crate>` leaves in `<cargo home>/bin`, per crate. Windows adds `.exe`.

Family.description: Every node of the closure of the root task `setup`, with the answer to the five questions: is the output cacheable, is it looked up in the fleet before it runs, is it uploaded after, what is host-bound, which class. `lookup` and `upload` name the mechanism that does it today: `install-pack` (fleet install packs), `blob` (pinned download by sha256), `mirror` (the group server's package mirror), `setup-record` (this module), `nx` (Nx remote cache of a cached task) or `none`.
